### 1) What is on the screen
The frame is a sprite-scale test card on solid black, not a gameplay screen. Top-center is the word OURANOS. Bottom row left to right are four versions of the same white-bearded robed figure at 1X, 2X, 3X, 4X with small labels 1X 2X 3X 4X underneath. The eye goes first to the largest 4X figure in region x,y,width,height 163,110,56,96 because it is the biggest high-contrast shape. The player is being asked to do nothing - I cannot see a level, HUD, enemies, objective, or controls.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES - PASS: measured 3 distinct colours, well inside the 25 colours on screen ceiling, measured as all valid 64-entry NES palette, reads as 1-bit + grey.
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape - PASS: beard white, robe grey, no gradient banding visible.
(c) sprites read at a glance against background - PASS: white/grey on 90.1% black backdrop gives clean silhouette, no muddy shared colours.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges - PASS: text and sprites show hard 1px steps, no blur, no alpha, as required with no rotation, no alpha.
(e) background colour changes land on 16x16 grid - PASS: background is solid with no attribute drift; trivially passes because there is no background tile variation to violate the 16x16 pixel boundary rule.
Measured numbers do not contradict impression - it is technically legal at 256x240, multiple of 8, 8x8 tiles capable, 64 OAM capable, 8 per scanline capable. It just does not look like a shipped game frame, it looks like a test ROM.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded nowhere. Empty almost everywhere: top 0,32,256,100 and middle are void. All weight is in a bottom strip roughly 27,110,200,102. Focal point 163,110,56,96 is where the eye lands, but there is no gameplay need for it there. Text regions: T1 OURANOS at 97,15,67,14, T2 labels row 27,210,200,12 split into 1X at 30,212,16,10, 2X at 68,212,16,10, 3X at 119,212,16,10, 4X at 172,212,16,10. All legible at 256x240 without guessing. Worst is T2 1X at 30,212,16,10 - legible but cramped against the tiny 14px-tall sprite above it with only ~4px gap, and at real CRT distance the 1X glyphs will buzz.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
No AI tells. No pillow shading, no detail without structure, no mangled glyphs, no non-tile borders, no stray pixels, no off-palette colours. Integer scaling looks honest and handmade. What is off is that this is a composition that reads as an asset viewer, not a design: huge empty backdrop, no ground, no 16x16 attribute zones used, no window, no status. I cannot see scrolling, tilemap, or sprite-zero use.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Region [0,40,256,96]: fill void with repeating 8x8 star tile using backdrop NES $0F Black + 1px NES $30 White dots on every 16px, to prove background plane and remove 90% empty.
2. Region [0,196,256,16]: add 8px-high ground strip two tiles tall, solid NES $00 Dark Grey top row + NES $0F Black bottom row, aligned to 8px grid, and place all four figures' feet on y=196.
3. Region [97,15,67,14]: move OURANOS down by 8 pixels to [97,23,67,14] so cap-height sits on an 8px tile row, redraw in 8x8 glyphs using only NES $30 White on $0F Black.
4. Region [30,182,14,24]: delete 1X figure - at 8x8 or 8x16 sprite limit it is unreadable as a character; replace with 16x16 2-tile icon or leave blank, do not keep sub-readable sprite.
5. Region [163,110,56,96]: on 4X figure recolor robe shadow pixels from NES $10 Light Grey to NES $00 Dark Grey, keep beard NES $30 White, to give 2-value sprite-palette separation instead of white-on-light-grey.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
nes_authenticity: 7 - legal but test card, not game.
readability: 8 - high contrast, legible.
charm: 4 - cute wizard, wasted frame.
